anchor_rules_checkable.TR-1_creation: The anchor is created ONLY by the privileged setup role, O_EXCL, inside the anchor namespace, before the capture's first transport call. It binds: capture_id, genesis nonce, journal (dev,ino), control-dir (dev,ino), genesis chain hash, status=ACTIVE, head=genesis hash. The executor NEVER creates, replaces, renames or deletes an anchor; there is no executor code path that writes the anchor namespace.
anchor_rules_checkable.TR-2_ownership_permissions: Anchor namespace directory: owner = setup role (root or dedicated anchor uid), mode 0755 (or stricter). Anchor file: owner = setup role, mode 0444. Executor uid: read-only traversal + read. Any write/rename/unlink attempt by a non-owner is a kernel EPERM, not an application check.
anchor_rules_checkable.TR-3_no_replacement: An anchor is never replaced in place. A new capture (including capture-id reuse) is a NEW anchor installed by the setup role, which first retires the previous one. Retirement and sealing are the only post-creation transitions, both performed by privileged roles: ACTIVE --(finalizer seal: status=SEALED, head=terminal chain hash)--> SEALED --(setup role)--> RETIRED.
anchor_rules_checkable.TR-4_restart_resolution: Restart reads the anchor ONLY from the anchor namespace (never from the data tree), then resolves journal/control by the anchored (dev,ino) bindings plus genesis hash + nonce FROM THE ANCHOR. A data-tree identity object, if present at all, is not consulted. If the canonical control path does not resolve to the anchored inode, restart scans for the anchored inode under renamed entries and returns HOLD:CONTROL_REPLACED with the consumed state read from the anchored journal inode -- it never adopts a replacement world as current.
anchor_rules_checkable.TR-5_replay: If anchor status is SEALED, restart requires the resolved journal's chain head to equal the anchor's sealed head; anything else is HOLD:REPLAY. If a prior generation's anchor is RETIRED, no artifact from that generation can satisfy TR-4 for the current capture.
anchor_rules_checkable.TR-6_fences: During a live run, fences (open / append / pre-call after ATTEMPT fsync / finalize / complete) re-read the anchor from the namespace and compare against the in-memory copy obtained at open. The in-memory copy is a cache, never a root: it is validated against the namespace at open, and the namespace cannot change under the modeled adversary.
anchor_rules_checkable.TR-7_recovery: Anchor missing, unparsable, or binding-mismatched at restart => HOLD:ANCHOR_MISSING / HOLD:IDENTITY_MISMATCH and zero transport calls. Recovery is exclusively out-of-band: a fresh setup-role install under separate user/production authority, after human adjudication of the data-tree state. The executor never self-rebinds, never regenerates an anchor, never treats a missing anchor as a fresh capture.
anchor_rules_checkable.TR-8_vocabulary: The word 'immutable' is retired. The checkable properties are: created-by (setup role only), writable-by (no one at runtime; transitions only via privileged roles), replaceable-by (kernel EPERM for every non-owner), verifiable-at (restart, from the namespace alone + the data tree it binds).

defect_corrected: r5 anchored trust in <capture_id>.identity.json, a pathname object inside the same mutable archive-parent namespace it polices. O_EXCL gives creation exclusivity, not post-creation immutability; restart (OC-7) read the canonical identity pathname and trusted the bindings, nonce and genesis hash found inside it, so a coherent replacement of identity+control+journal after owner exit presents a self-consistent new world and is accepted as fresh. The anchor itself needed an anchor (regress).

closes: T9 (data-tree bundle cannot rewrite the bindings restart trusts)
T10 (anchor carries status + sealed terminal head installed by the finalizer role; prior-generation or prefix state cannot match it)
A_PRIVILEGED_ANCHOR_NAMESPACE.costs: One-time privileged setup per deployment + a privileged install act per capture + a privileged seal act per completion. No cryptography, no key custody.
A_PRIVILEGED_ANCHOR_NAMESPACE.mechanism: Identity anchor installed in a directory owned by a privileged setup role (root or a dedicated anchor uid), mode 0755 root-owned dir / 0444 anchor file. The capture executor and any process at its privilege level hold NO write or rename rights in that directory (rename requires write on the containing directory, so pathname replacement is impossible, not merely detectable).
A_PRIVILEGED_ANCHOR_NAMESPACE.portability: Any POSIX filesystem with uid separation. No kernel features beyond discretionary permissions.

closes: T8 (empty/forged content fails signature; byte-identical copy is the same self-authenticating content)
B_DETACHED_SIGNATURE.costs: Key generation, custody, rotation and loss procedures; a signer act per capture and per seal; compromise of the signer key collapses the root silently.
does_not_close: T10 prior-generation replay: a GENUINE older signed bundle verifies perfectly. A signature proves authenticity, not freshness or currency. The current generation's existence is invisible to a pathname-read signed identity unless an external monotonic registry exists -- which is design A's namespace by another name.
B_DETACHED_SIGNATURE.mechanism: Identity object stays in the data tree but carries a detached signature over its canonical core, produced by a signer role whose key is unavailable to the executor/path adversary; the executor pins the verification key (provenance: the adopted rev3 manifest pin, an artifact in a different trust domain, never read from the data tree).

closes: T8 partially (in-place content tamper of the genuine file is detected)
C_FS_VERITY_IMMUTABILITY.costs: ext4/btrfs/f2fs + kernel >= 5.4 for verity; enabling verity or +i is itself a privileged/finalizing act; the journal (append-only, mutated all run) can never be verity-protected, only the static identity object can. Poor portability.
does_not_close: T9/T10: fs-verity authenticates a file against a digest, but at restart the expected digest has to come from somewhere. If it comes from the journal GENESIS, the adversary authors both sides of the comparison (modeled: F_VERITY fails T9 and T10 exactly as the pathname design does). If the digest is pinned in a privileged store, the design has silently become design A with extra machinery.
Rename-away + replacement at the same pathname is unaffected by per-file immutability.
C_FS_VERITY_IMMUTABILITY.mechanism: Identity file made content-immutable after creation via fs-verity (Merkle root fixed at enable time) or the immutable flag.

residual_trust_assumptions.TCB-1: The OS kernel's uid/permission enforcement and the integrity of the privileged accounts (root / anchor uid / finalizer role). An adversary who IS root, or who can write the anchor namespace, is OUTSIDE this contract's adversary model; against a hostile root nothing here holds, and the contract says so rather than implying otherwise.
residual_trust_assumptions.TCB-2: The setup and finalizer roles act honestly at install and seal time. Both acts require separate user/production authority (see readiness separation); they are human-gated operations, not executor behavior.
residual_trust_assumptions.TCB-3: The path by which the executor locates the anchor namespace is resolved at process start from configuration under the deployment's control (absolute path). If a PARENT component of that path is adversary-renamed, resolution lands on a nonexistent path (HOLD:ANCHOR_MISSING) or on a directory whose anchor fails the capture binding (HOLD) -- fail-closed in both cases, never silent acceptance, because anchor contents are owner-controlled and capture-bound.
residual_trust_assumptions.TCB-4: (dev,ino) values are never trusted alone: inode numbers recycle. Every binding is (dev,ino) + genesis hash + nonce as recorded in the anchor (clause OC-12 from r5 is retained and now rooted outside the data tree).
residual_trust_assumptions.TCB-5: Local POSIX filesystem semantics (ext4-class). Network filesystems (NFS etc.) are out of assumption, as in r5.
residual_trust_assumptions.TCB-6: The executor's own in-memory state during a single live run, between fences, exactly as bounded in r5.

what_remains_provable_when_root_conteste: If the anchor namespace itself is contested (TCB-1 violated), NOTHING about restart state is provable from filesystem artifacts alone, and the contract's answer is a HOLD with zero transport calls pending out-of-band adjudication -- safety (no duplicate calls, no foreign state adopted) is preserved by refusing to proceed; availability is not, and is not claimed.
